newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish crown continues to firm, debt yields fall.
newsitem.headline: Swedish crown continues to firm, debt yields fall.

text.p: Swedish debt yields fell a touch on Monday by midday and the crown softened in the aftermath of the French left-wing victory.
"We tried to follow Germany and take yields up in the morning, but it did just not hold. The market is still strong," one dealer said.
"If anything should be sold it's German and Italian risk, since they going to be in EMU," he said.
The ruling Swedish Social Democrats will present their standpoint on EMU, Europe's economic and monetary union, at a news conference at 1430 GMT on June 3.
The market was focussing on their view, which was expected to be a soft no.
Six-month T-bill rates shed four basis points to 4.26 percent and the ten-year bond yields dropped one basis point to 7.05. The crown firmed to 4.5155 against the mark from 4.5335 late on Friday.

Given the good Swedish fundamentals and the fact the the flows of redeemed bond coupons and dividends are ebbing out, Nordbanken said it sees a strengthening to 4.40 against the mark by year-end, staying in the 4.30-4.50 range against the mark.
